newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Rally keeps focus on broad market.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Rally keeps focus on broad market.

text.p: Investors focused less on individual equity options than on the broad market as the stock market rallied sharply, but some large trades crossed in a few issues, traders said Tuesday.
"We're kind of slow down here," one trader in New York said, referring to equity options activity at the American Stock Exchange.

In late trading, the Dow industrial average .DJI was up 173 points at 6,956, just a few points off its session high. The S&P 500 index was up 20 points at 793 and June S&P 500 futures rallied 23.20 points to 798.40.
"I think everybody's watching the market," one broker in Chicago said. "We've been pretty quiet" on the equity option side.
He said the heaviest options trading appeared to be concentrated in single options as opposed to a group of options in one stock.
An investor bought 9,000 of the Nabisco Holdings Corp May 35 calls at 2-3/4 and sold 10,000 of the May 35 puts at 5/16, said Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co.
The May 35 call had open interest of 1,718 and the May 35 put had open interest of 1,243.
Some of the heaviest equity options trading was in Microsoft Corp, where the May 115 call traded more than 12,000 contracts alone. The option, which was up 2-1/4 at six, had open interest of 8,581.
Microsoft shares were up four at 118-7/8, moving through the 115 strike price. Turnover was about 8.8 million.
Other busy Microsoft options included the May 120 calls and the May 110, 115 and 120 puts.
In other trading, the Telebras May 115 call traded a total of about 10,600 contracts. The bulk of the action was on the AMEX, where about 7,800 crossed.
The options are traded on the AMEX, the Chicago Board Options Exchange and the Philadelphia Stock Exchange.
Telebras shares gained 1-1/2 to 112-5/8 on turnover of 1.4 million shares.
